source: Thirty-three ways to read the same numbers, each a published rule of thumb or one of Eli's own, stated as a rule, a band and three sentences. 50/30/20 (Elizabeth Warren), the Money Guy Show's 25% and rate-by-age, Ramit Sethi's conscious spending, Your Money or Your Life (Robin and Dominguez), Die With Zero (Bill Perkins), the Bogleheads three-fund portfolio, the bucket strategy, the 20/3/8 car rule, Mr. Money Mustache's Shockingly Simple Math, the FOO (the Money Guy Show's Financial Order of Operations) and the DRAFTT letters. Each lens re-reads DAITE numbers already in the household; no lens adds a field.
confidenceNote: Rules of thumb, not findings. A lens says what a well-known framework would say about your numbers, in one sentence, and then says who it is for and who it is not for. The second pair is the advice translator: a lens without it does not ship.
note: Read by shared/lenses.js (SLAF.Lenses — the name Lens is the four-way $ / hours / bought / pushed toggle, D-094). Each domain shows its `default` lens; the rest render only behind the "More ways to look at this" toggle, off by default. `band` is on the measure's own basis (the `measure` note says which); null means the lens states a number and has one verdict sentence. `verdict` is [under, in, over] for a banded lens, [sentence] for the rest; {tokens} are filled by the library from the measure. `plain` is the header when the showFrameworkNames preference is off. D-175.

lenses.name: FAT and wants
lenses.plain: Needs inside half of take-home
lenses.rule: Food, a roof and getting around inside half of take-home; the rest is wants and saving.
lenses.measure: needs, a share of take-home a month
verdict: Needs take {share} of take-home — under half, with room to spare.
Needs take {share} of take-home: {amount} a month on food, a roof and getting around, inside half.
Needs take {share} of take-home, over half: the three lines leave little for wants or saving.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with take-home pay and the three needs lines filled in.
lenses.notForWhom: Between jobs, with no take-home to divide: read the runway instead.

lenses.plain: A fifth of take-home saved
lenses.rule: Half of take-home to needs, three-tenths to wants, a fifth saved or paid down.
lenses.measure: what is left of take-home after spending, a share of take-home
verdict: {share} of take-home is left after spending, under the 20 the rule wants.
{share} of take-home is left after spending — the 20 is met.
{share} of take-home is left after spending, well past the 20.
lenses.forWhom: Someone starting out who wants three numbers and no spreadsheet.
lenses.notForWhom: High earners in expensive cities: the 50 for needs is often impossible on rent alone, and the 20 is too little.

lenses.name: Money Guy 25%
lenses.plain: Save a quarter of what you earn
lenses.rule: Save 25% of gross for retirement.
lenses.measure: retirement contributions, a share of gross
verdict: Under. You're at {share} of gross.
There: {share} of gross.
Above, good: {share} of gross.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a job and no high-interest debt.
lenses.notForWhom: Carrying credit card debt: clear it first, this comes later.

lenses.name: Conscious spending
lenses.plain: One rich-life line, ruthless on the rest
lenses.rule: Spend without guilt on the one thing you love; be ruthless on everything else. Guilt-free spending runs 20 to 35% of take-home.
lenses.measure: wants, a share of take-home a month
verdict: Wants are {share} of take-home: under the 20 Ramit says to spend on purpose — the plan may be too tight to keep.
Wants are {share} of take-home, inside the 20 to 35 the plan allows.
Wants are {share} of take-home, over the 35: pick the one line that is your rich life and be ruthless on the rest.
lenses.forWhom: Someone who hates budgets and wants one line to protect.
lenses.notForWhom: A month that does not close: the ruthless part comes before the guilt-free part.
lenses.source: Ramit Sethi, I Will Teach You to Be Rich

lenses.name: Your Money or Your Life
lenses.plain: A month of spending, in hours of your life
lenses.rule: Every dollar is life energy: price each line in the hours of work it costs at your real hourly wage.
lenses.measure: hours of life a month of spending costs
verdict: A month of spending is {hours} hours of your life at {wage} an hour — about {hoursWeek} hours a week of work.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who has filled in Real Hourly Wage and wonders whether a line is worth it.
lenses.notForWhom: Retired or between jobs: with no wage there are no hours to price in.

lenses.name: Die With Zero
lenses.plain: Spend when you can use it
lenses.rule: Net worth should peak somewhere between 45 and 60 and be spent down after: experiences pay a memory dividend, and a pile at the end is life unspent.
lenses.measure: your age against the peak window
verdict: At {age}, these are the building years: spend on experiences that pay memory dividends now, while they are cheap and you are able.
At {age}, Die With Zero says net worth should be peaking about now and spending should start to climb.
At {age}, the pile should be shrinking on purpose: spending it is the plan, not a failure of it.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a date of birth entered and a fear of dying rich.
lenses.notForWhom: A household with no cushion yet: the book assumes the basics are covered before the spending curve starts.

lenses.name: Avalanche
lenses.plain: Highest rate first
lenses.rule: Every spare dollar to the highest rate; minimums on the rest. Cheapest in interest.
lenses.measure: the highest rate you carry, against the high-interest line
verdict: No debt above the line.
Nothing above {threshold}: minimums and invest — the avalanche has no target here.
{top} at {rate} first: it is above the {threshold} line, and every spare dollar there saves the most interest.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who can keep paying a plan without seeing a balance disappear.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone who needs an early win to keep going: see the snowball.

lenses.name: Snowball
lenses.plain: Smallest balance first
lenses.rule: Smallest balance first, whatever its rate, for the win that keeps you going.
lenses.measure: the smallest balance and how fast its minimum clears it
verdict: Smallest first: {label} at {balance} — about {months} at its minimum alone, sooner with anything extra. Its rate is {rate}, so it costs {costNote}.
lenses.forWhom: Someone with several debts who needs one gone to believe the rest can go.
lenses.notForWhom: One big debt at a high rate: there is nothing to snowball; see the avalanche.

lenses.name: Money Guy rate by age
lenses.plain: Pay it off or invest, by your decade
lenses.rule: Pay off a debt above the threshold for your decade; invest instead of prepaying the rest.
lenses.measure: the highest rate you carry, against your decade's threshold
verdict: No debt to weigh.
Nothing above {threshold}, the line for your {decade}: invest rather than prepay.
{top} at {rate} is above {threshold}, the line for your {decade}: pay it off before investing more.
lenses.forWhom: Someone with a low-rate loan wondering whether to prepay it or invest.
lenses.notForWhom: Credit card debt at any age: that is always above the line.

lenses.name: Payoff-vs-invest crossover
lenses.plain: The rate where investing wins
lenses.rule: Below the return you assume on investments, investing wins on paper; above it, paying off is the guaranteed win.
lenses.measure: the highest rate you carry, against your assumed real return
verdict: No debt to weigh.
Every rate you carry is under {crossover}, the real return you assume: investing wins on paper, with more risk.
{top} at {rate} beats the {crossover} you assume on investments: paying it off is the sure thing. {aboveCount} of your {count} debts are above the line.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone choosing between an extra payment and an extra contribution.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone without an emergency fund: neither wins until the cushion exists.

lenses.name: DRAFTT D
lenses.plain: Debt payments, a share of take-home
lenses.rule: Non-mortgage minimums under a tenth of take-home.
lenses.measure: non-mortgage minimums, a share of take-home
verdict: Under.
Minimums are {share} of take-home, inside the band.
Minimums are {share} of take-home, over the band: the month is carrying yesterday's spending.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with debts entered and a take-home figure.
lenses.notForWhom: A mortgage only: it sits in A, not here.

lenses.name: FOO position
lenses.plain: The next thing money should do
lenses.rule: Money has an order: basics, starter fund, the match, high-interest debt, the full fund, HSA, Roth, the rest of the tax-advantaged space, then everything else.
lenses.measure: the first step not yet met
verdict: Step {step}: {label}.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone unsure what the next dollar should do.
lenses.notForWhom: Retired: the ladder is for building, not drawing down.

lenses.name: Three-fund check
lenses.plain: Stocks, world stocks, bonds — and roughly how much bond
lenses.rule: A total-market fund, an international fund and a bond fund, with bonds somewhere between a tenth and four-tenths while you are still earning.
lenses.measure: bonds, a share of the target mix
verdict: Bonds at {share}: lighter than most three-fund mixes — fine if you can sit through a fall without selling.
Bonds at {share}, in the usual range; stocks at {stocks}.
Bonds at {share}: heavier than most three-fund mixes for someone still earning.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a target mix in Where It Goes.
lenses.notForWhom: Money you need in under five years: it is not in stocks or bonds at all.

lenses.name: Bucket strategy
lenses.plain: Years of spending in cash
lenses.rule: One to three years of spending in cash, the next several in bonds, the rest in stocks, so a bad year never forces a sale.
lenses.measure: years of spending held in cash
verdict: {years} of spending in cash: under a year, so a bad market and a bad year at work would hit at once.
{years} of spending in cash, inside the first bucket.
{years} of spending in cash: more than three years, which is safety paid for in growth.
lenses.forWhom: Someone near or in retirement, or anyone who wants to know how long the cash lasts.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone still on the starter emergency fund: one bucket first.

lenses.name: Asset location
lenses.plain: Pre-tax, Roth or taxable, by your bracket
lenses.rule: In a higher bracket now than later, pre-tax first; in a lower one, Roth first; taxable takes what is left.
lenses.measure: pre-tax, a share of retirement money, read against your marginal rate
verdict: At a {marginal} marginal rate, pre-tax is {share} of your retirement money ({roth} Roth, {taxable} taxable): light for the bracket — pre-tax would take the deduction now.
At a {marginal} marginal rate, pre-tax is {share} of your retirement money, Roth {roth}, taxable {taxable}: a reasonable mix for the bracket.
At a {marginal} marginal rate, pre-tax is {share} of your retirement money ({roth} Roth, {taxable} taxable): heavy for the bracket — Roth would lock in today's lower rate.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone whose accounts say how they are taxed, in the Statement.
lenses.notForWhom: An account entered as one total: say how it is taxed first.

lenses.name: Glide path by FI stage
lenses.plain: How much in stocks, by how far along you are
lenses.rule: Start near 90% stocks and glide to about 60% as the target comes into view: the closer you are, the less a fall may cost.
lenses.measure: stocks, a share of the target mix, against the share the stage suggests
verdict: Stocks at {share}: {progress} of the way to the target suggests about {suggested} — you are lighter than that.
Stocks at {share}: {progress} of the way to the target suggests about {suggested}, and you are near it.
Stocks at {share}: {progress} of the way to the target suggests about {suggested} — a fall now would cost more than it needs to.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a FIRE number, an investment balance and a target mix.
lenses.notForWhom: Money with a date on it: a glide path is for the long pot only.

lenses.name: Coast FI check
lenses.plain: Enough invested to stop adding
lenses.rule: Once what you have would grow to the full number by your target age on its own, contributions become optional.
lenses.measure: what you have, a share of the coast number
verdict: {invested} of the {coast} coast number: {share} of the way. Not at coast yet — contributions still do the work until {target}.
Past coast: what you have grows to the full number by {target} on its own.
Past coast: what you have grows to the full number by {target} on its own.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who wants to know when saving becomes optional.
lenses.notForWhom: Retired: coast is a milestone on the way, not a way to draw down.

lenses.name: Total cost of ownership
lenses.plain: Getting around, a month
lenses.rule: The whole line — payment, fuel, insurance, upkeep, parking, transit — under a tenth of take-home.
lenses.measure: getting around, a share of take-home a month
verdict: Under.
Getting around costs {amount} a month, {share} of take-home, inside a tenth.
Getting around costs {amount} a month, {share} of take-home, over a tenth: the second-biggest line to attack after housing.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with the transportation line filled in.
lenses.notForWhom: A household with no vehicle and no transit cost: the line is legitimately near zero.

lenses.plain: A car payment under 8% of gross
lenses.rule: 20% down, a loan no longer than three years, and the payment under 8% of gross monthly income.
lenses.measure: the whole getting-around line, a share of gross a month — strict by design, since the rule is for the payment alone
verdict: Under.
Getting around is {share} of gross, inside the 8: at your income the rule allows a car of about {maxPrice} on a three-year loan.
Getting around is {share} of gross, over the 8 — and that is the whole line, not just a payment. The rule allows about {maxPrice} of car.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone about to finance a car.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone paying cash for a car they will keep ten years: the rule is about loans.

lenses.name: Car as a share of net worth
lenses.plain: What your cars are worth, against everything
lenses.rule: Vehicles under about 15% of net worth: they lose value every year and the rest of the sheet should not.
lenses.measure: vehicles, a share of net worth
verdict: Under.
Your vehicles are {amount}, {share} of net worth, inside the band.
Your vehicles are {amount}, {share} of net worth: a large slice of what you own is losing value every year.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who has entered a vehicle in the Statement.
lenses.notForWhom: A negative net worth: the share has no meaning; read the debt lenses first.

lenses.name: Return on Hassle
lenses.plain: Is the cheaper way worth your hours?
lenses.rule: A cheaper option that costs you hours must save more than those hours earn at your real hourly wage.
lenses.measure: the bar any hassle has to clear: your real hourly wage
verdict: An hour of your life earns {wage} after tax and the costs of working. A cheaper way to get around that costs you an hour a week must save more than {weekly} a week — about {monthly} a month — to be worth it.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone weighing the bus, a longer drive, a cheaper car or fixing it yourself.
lenses.notForWhom: No wage yet: the bar is not set until Real Hourly Wage is.

lenses.name: 25% of gross
lenses.plain: Housing under a quarter of what you earn
lenses.rule: Rent or mortgage, tax and insurance under a quarter of gross.
lenses.measure: the accommodation line, a share of gross a month
verdict: Under.
Housing is {amount} a month, {share} of gross, inside the quarter.
Housing is {amount} a month, {share} of gross, over the quarter: the biggest line, and the one that moves everything else.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a rent or mortgage line.
lenses.notForWhom: A paid-off home: the line is tax and insurance only, and the quarter does not apply.

lenses.name: Rent-vs-buy breakeven
lenses.plain: How many years before buying wins
lenses.rule: Buying wins once the years of unrecoverable-cost savings pay back the closing costs; under that, renting wins.
lenses.measure: years until owning's savings repay the closing costs
verdict: Owning pays back its closing costs at once.
Owning breaks even in about {years}: stay longer than that and buying wins on the unrecoverable costs alone.
Breakeven is {years} away: renting wins unless you stay longer than that.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a price and a rent typed into Housing Decision.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone who may move in under five years: see the 5-year rule.

lenses.name: House hack
lenses.plain: Cut the biggest line by sharing it
lenses.rule: A housemate, a smaller place or a cheaper town cuts the accommodation line by 40% — the lever's figure, read from the lever library.
lenses.measure: what the house-hack lever is worth on your line, a month and an hour
verdict: The house hack would take about {gain} a month off your {line} line — about {hourly} an hour for the {hours} hours a week it costs. {applies}
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a property, or a price typed in Housing Decision.
lenses.notForWhom: A lease with no room to share and no move in sight: the lever does not apply yet.

lenses.name: 5-year rule
lenses.plain: Do not buy if you may move within five years
lenses.rule: Closing costs on the way in and selling costs on the way out together run near a tenth of the price; under five years they rarely come back.
lenses.measure: the round trip: buying and selling costs on the price you are weighing
verdict: On {price}, the round trip — closing costs in, agent and closing costs out — is about {roundTrip}. Under five years, appreciation rarely covers it; rent if a move is likely.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone weighing a price in Housing Decision.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone who has already owned the place for years: the costs are sunk.

lenses.name: DRAFTT A
lenses.plain: Rent or mortgage, a share of take-home
lenses.rule: One number, a month, under a quarter of take-home.
lenses.measure: the accommodation line, a share of take-home
verdict: Under.
Housing is {share} of take-home, inside the band.
Housing is {share} of take-home, over the band.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a rent or mortgage line and take-home pay.
lenses.notForWhom: A paid-off home.

lenses.name: Take-home
lenses.plain: What you keep of what you earn
lenses.rule: Gross is the headline; take-home is what the month is actually made of.
lenses.measure: take-home, a share of gross
verdict: You keep {share} of what you earn: {takeHome} a month from {gross}, after about {tax} a year of tax. Every share in this room is of the {takeHome}.
lenses.forWhom: Everyone with an income and a filing status.
lenses.notForWhom: Nobody — but self-employed take-home here is before quarterly estimates you set aside yourself.

lenses.name: Real Hourly Wage
lenses.plain: What an hour of your life really earns
lenses.rule: Pay after tax and the costs of working, over every hour the job takes — commute, prep and unwinding included.
lenses.measure: your real hourly wage against the one on paper
verdict: {real} an hour, really, against {nominal} on paper: the job takes {hours} hours a week once the commute and the rest are counted.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with a job and a commute.
lenses.notForWhom: Retired or between jobs: there is no wage to correct.

lenses.name: Savings rate
lenses.plain: What you save of what you earn
lenses.rule: Take-home less spending, over gross. The one number that sets the FI date.
lenses.measure: what is saved, a share of gross
verdict: You save {share} of gross, under 15: the FI date is far, and the rate — not the return — is what moves it.
You save {share} of gross: past 15, and every point moves the date.
You save {share} of gross: past 15, and every point moves the date.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone with income, spending and a filing status entered.
lenses.notForWhom: Variable income: read the rolling average first, then this.

lenses.name: Shockingly Simple Math
lenses.plain: Years to FI from the savings rate alone
lenses.rule: Your savings rate, and nothing else, sets the years to FI: from zero, at the real return you assume, until 25 years of spending is in the pot.
lenses.measure: years to FI from zero at your savings rate
verdict: At {share} saved, {years} years to FI from zero at {returnRate} real. Ten points more makes it {yearsPlus}.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone who wants the one lever that matters most.
lenses.notForWhom: Someone already holding a pot: the FIRE room counts what you have; this starts from nothing on purpose.

lenses.name: Effective vs marginal
lenses.plain: Your average rate and your next-dollar rate
lenses.rule: The average rate is what your life is taxed at; the marginal rate is what a raise is taxed at. They are different numbers and people mix them up.
lenses.measure: the effective rate, with the marginal beside it
verdict: Your average rate is about {effective}; the next dollar is taxed at {marginal}. A raise is taxed at the second, your life at the first.
lenses.forWhom: Everyone with an income and a filing status.
lenses.notForWhom: Nobody — but a self-employed picture adds the self-employment tax the table already includes.

lenses.name: The four buckets
lenses.plain: Pre-tax, Roth, taxable, HSA — which is empty
lenses.rule: Four places to hold money, taxed four ways. Most people have one; the flexibility later comes from having several.
lenses.measure: how many of the four buckets hold something or receive something
verdict: {filled} of four in use: {filledList}. Empty: {emptyList}. Each empty one is a tax rate you cannot choose later.
{filled} of four in use: {filledList}. Empty: {emptyList}.
All four in use: {filledList}.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone whose accounts say how they are taxed.
lenses.notForWhom: No HSA eligibility: three buckets is the full set for you.

lenses.name: Bracket headroom
lenses.plain: How much more fits in your bracket
lenses.rule: The room left before the next bracket: what a Roth conversion, a bonus or a side income can add at today's marginal rate.
lenses.measure: income that fits before the next bracket
verdict: About {room} more taxable income fits in the {marginal} bracket before the {next} one starts.
lenses.forWhom: Anyone weighing a Roth conversion, a bonus or extra work this year.
lenses.notForWhom: The top bracket: there is no next one.
